names_for.catalogue_side: data products with a public offer, listed in the "AWS Marketplace product catalog" (browsed via "Browse catalog")
names_for.custom_side: "custom offers" ("private offers" and "Bring Your Own Subscription (BYOS) offers") and "private products"; AWS itself does no bespoke collection, and "Request data product" routes a buyer to the "Data Discovery Team" for recommendations

operator_role.note: AWS is not a party to the DSA or buyer-seller agreements and the provider's account is seller of record, but AWS invoices the buyer, collects and disburses net of fees.

economics_model.note: Percentage listing fee on contract value; data grants (no marketplace) are instead billed per active grant-hour plus storage.

who_pays_fee.note: Listing fee is deducted from the seller's disbursement; data-grant hourly fee is paid by the sender; buyers pay only their own AWS infrastructure usage.

supply_models.note: Third-party providers list only data sets they own; Open Data on AWS public data sets are also findable. AWS does not list its own collected data.

custody_model.note: Files: AWS-hosted copy exported to buyer's S3; S3 data access / Redshift / Lake Formation: shared in place from the provider's own storage.

transaction_mode.note: Self-serve subscription to public offers; private offers negotiated off-platform and accepted in console.

public_prices.note: Public offers show prices; private offer prices are not public; many image listings are free samples with full data on request.

licence_model.note: Default standard DSA template, but the provider controls terms and may edit or replace it.

exclusivity_offered.note: Standard DSA licence is non-exclusive [c063]; nothing found on whether custom DSAs grant exclusivity.

public_listing.note: Product detail pages on AWS Marketplace were fetched without login; data set descriptions are visible only to active subscribers.

buyer_vetting.note: An AWS account suffices by default; providers may switch on subscription verification to review each subscriber.

sample_mechanics.note: Optional provider-uploaded samples and dictionaries downloadable before subscribing; many providers also list free sample products.

versioning.note: Files revisions are immutable once finalized; S3 data access shares are live and need no new revision [c102].

human_subject_consent_docs.note: Provider warrants personal data is public and indemnifies for missing consents; no consent or release documents are delivered to buyers by the platform.

contributor_pay_model.note: No contributor programme; supply comes from registered provider businesses paid monthly disbursements.

catalogue_plus_custom.note: Custom work is provider-run via private offers/private products; AWS offers recommendation, not bespoke collection.

erasure_after_sale.note: Default DSA requires removal within 90 days of end; exported files otherwise remain with buyer.

quality_evidence.note: AWS reviews listings for policy compliance, not data quality; samples and descriptions come from the provider.

Q1.answer: No demand volumes are published; for photo and image data, listings seen are free samples with the full or custom corpus sold by contacting the provider. Buyers who cannot find data can file a request with budget and cadence.

Q2.answer: Listing gives the provider AWS billing, entitlement and delivery plumbing, catalogue reach (vendor-stated 3,500+ products) and free migration of existing subscribers; it costs a 3% listing fee and requires seller registration, ADX qualification and an eligible jurisdiction.

Q3.answer: Only registered providers list, and only data sets their own account owns; the DSA contemplates resold third-party data under extra terms. Open Data on AWS public data sets are also surfaced.

Q4.answer: Not a commissioning platform, so no resale carve-outs; on term changes, an auto-renewing subscription renews onto the new price and DSA.

Q5.answer: AWS is a venue: the DSA is solely between provider and subscriber, AWS is not a party, the provider is seller of record and warrants and indemnifies; AWS invoices and collects.

Q6.answer: Mixed: Files products are copied into AWS Data Exchange and exported to the buyer's S3; S3 data access shares read-only from the provider's own bucket through an AWS-provisioned access point, revoked when the subscription ends.

Q7.answer: Guidelines ban identifiable personal data outside the Extended Provider Program and require sensitive categories anonymised; the DSA has the provider warrant public-only personal data and indemnify for missing consents. Nothing addresses capturer, depicted-person or property releases as documents.

Q8.answer: Default DSA: non-exclusive, worldwide, no redistribution, no re-identification, buyer owns derived data incl. models, deletion within 90 days of end, NY law; providers may substitute their own terms. No audit or fingerprinting mechanism found.

Q9.answer: Public offers are self-serve subscriptions paid upfront or on schedule; private and BYOS offers handle negotiated deals. AWS takes a listing fee (3% public; 3/2/1.5% private by contract value; 1.5% renewals) deducted from disbursement.

Q10.answer: Product > data sets > revisions > assets; offers carry terms; a subscription yields entitled (read-only) data sets. Finalized revisions are immutable; the offer sets historical and future revision access; access ends at expiry; unpublishing keeps active subscribers; revisions can be revoked with a stated reason.

Q11.answer: Providers may attach up to 10 samples and data dictionaries viewable before purchase; listings must be accurate and flag anonymisation; AWS reviews for policy, while the DSA disclaims accuracy.

Q12.answer: The platform is the catalogue; custom deals run through provider private offers and 'private products', and image providers use free samples as a funnel to curated custom sets.

sections.positioning: AWS Data Exchange is AWS's data-sharing and data-marketplace service [c128]: data grants for direct sharing with any AWS account [c001][c007], and data products sold through AWS Marketplace [c002]. It went GA in November 2019 [c089]; AWS claims 3,500+ products from 300+ providers (vendor-stated) [c119].
sections.supply: Supply is third-party only: providers must be registered AWS Marketplace sellers qualified by the ADX team [c046], in an eligible jurisdiction [c045], and may list only data sets their own account owns [c049]. The FAQ's narrower US/EU rule conflicts with the docs [c094]. Indian sellers can list ADX products but only to Indian buyers [c115][c116], while the ADX jurisdiction list omits India [c045]. Image providers such as PIXTA list from their own stock libraries [c108].
sections.object_model: Assets sit in revisions, revisions in data sets, data sets in products [c021][c002]. Offers attach price, duration, DSA and refund policy [c006]. Subscribing creates read-only entitled data sets [c024]. Finalized revisions are immutable [c022]; the offer sets how many historical and future revisions a subscriber gets [c083]. S3 data access shares need no new revision when objects change [c102]. Grants and products are single-Region [c030].
sections.listing: Product pages carry descriptions, samples, logo and support contact [c005]; up to 10 samples [c103]; data dictionaries and samples are viewable before purchase [c085]. Data set descriptions are subscriber-only [c127]. Listings must note anonymisation [c043]. Real image listings are free samples [c107][c110].
sections.discovery: One catalogue across Regions [c010], filterable by category and data set type [c124]. A buyer who finds nothing can file a 'Request data product' with cadence and budget; the Data Discovery Team replies within 2 business days [c121][c122].
sections.trust: AWS reviews products against guidelines before listing [c003] and removes breaching products [c044]. Providers flag sensitive data categories shown on the product page [c086]. The DSA puts personal-data warranties [c067] and USD 5M insurance [c072] on the provider but disclaims accuracy [c075].
sections.transaction: Public offers are self-serve: pick a price and duration and pay upfront [c033]. Private offers target named accounts with an acceptance deadline [c105][c097]; BYOS migrates existing customers [c016][c061]. AWS invoices the buyer [c088] and pays the provider monthly after collection [c017][c018].
sections.pricing: Providers pay AWS a listing fee: 3% on ADX public offers [c050]; private offers 3%/2%/1.5% by contract value [c051][c052][c053]; renewals 1.5% [c054], on pre-tax TCV [c055], deducted from payouts [c126]. Data grants cost senders USD 0.04167 per active grant-hour [c058] plus storage [c059]. Prices are USD only [c032], durations 1-36 months [c031].
sections.licence: The default Data Subscription Agreement [c034] grants a non-exclusive, worldwide, non-transferable licence incl. derived data [c063], bans redistribution [c064] and re-identification [c065], lets buyers own derived models [c066], caps liability at 3x spend or USD 1M [c070] and uses NY law [c073]. AWS is not a party [c074][c118]; providers may replace it [c036].
sections.custody: Files products are copied into ADX and exported to the buyer's S3 [c013][c028]. S3 data access leaves data in the provider's bucket: ADX provisions an access point granting read-only access [c098][c025] without copies [c026], revoked at expiry [c099]. Requester Pays is recommended [c062]. Objects must be S3 Standard or Intelligent-Tiering [c100].
sections.vetting: Providers need a support organisation [c048], seller registration and ADX qualification [c046]. Identifiable personal data is barred unless public [c040]; sensitive categories must be anonymised [c041]; the Extended Provider Program adds review for sensitive data [c019][c020]. Buyers need only an AWS account unless the provider enables subscription verification [c015].
sections.contributor_pay: Not applicable: there is no contributor or crowd programme; supply comes from provider businesses that receive monthly disbursements net of listing fees [c017][c126].
sections.post_sale: Access ends when the subscription expires [c079][c096]; unpublishing does not cut off active subscribers [c080]. Providers can revoke a revision with a stated reason [c023][c092]. Exported files stay with the buyer [c082], but the default DSA requires deletion within 90 days of termination [c071]. Providers can notify subscribers of updates, delays and deprecations [c093].
sections.catalogue_custom: AWS runs only the catalogue. Custom deals run through provider private offers and 'private products' [c123][c016]. Image providers use free samples as a funnel: PIXTA offers to curate a specific set [c109], Shutterstock sells tailored datasets via sales [c111], InfoBay licenses its full corpus on request [c113].
sections.changes: Key dates: GA 2019-11-13 [c089]; revision revocation 2022-03-15 [c092]; S3 data access GA 2023-03-14 [c091]; data grants without seller registration 2023-12-14 [c090]; current listing fee schedule 2024-01-05 [c056]. On auto-renewal, changed terms and DSA apply [c081].
sections.demand: Demand evidence is thin and vendor-stated: 3,500+ products and 300+ providers [c119]; 80+ providers and 1,000+ products at launch, as relayed by press [c120].
sections.regulation: The publishing guidelines bar identifiable personal data unless publicly available, outside the Extended Provider Program [c040], and require biometric, health and other sensitive categories to be aggregated or anonymised [c041]. The default DSA bans re-identification [c065]. AWS tells buyers to do their own privacy-law due diligence [c011].

buyer_journey.step: Lands on the AWS Marketplace catalogue (single catalogue for all Regions), searches or filters by category and data set type such as Files or Access to Amazon S3.
Opens a product page without logging in: provider, descriptions, logo, support contact, sensitive-data flag, offer price/duration, DSA or EULA link and refund policy.
Evaluates free samples and data dictionaries before buying (for image providers, often a separate free sample product).
If nothing fits or the full dataset is not self-serve, contacts the provider for a private offer or custom set, or files a 'Request data product' to the Data Discovery Team.

Signs in with an AWS account and subscribes: chooses one price/duration, accepts the offer terms and DSA, pays upfront or on schedule; if the provider enabled subscription verification, first submits a request for approval.
AWS invoices the buyer and may share contact details with the provider; the buyer receives entitled read-only data sets.
Accesses data: exports Files revisions to their own S3 (optionally auto-export new revisions), or reads the provider's S3 bucket in place through an access point.
Holds a licence under the DSA (non-exclusive, no redistribution); at expiry access is revoked and DSA may require deletion of exported data within 90 days.

sources.quote: Once a subscription has expired, you can no longer view or export the data sets.

claims.statement: If a provider unpublishes a product, existing subscribers keep access to its data sets while their subscription is active but cannot auto-renew.

sources.quote: If a provider decides to unpublish a product, you still have access to the data sets as long as your subscription is active.

claims.statement: If offer terms have changed when an auto-renewing subscription renews, the new price and new DSA apply to the renewed subscription.

sources.quote: the new product offer terms (including new price and new DSA) apply

claims.statement: When a Files subscription ends the subscriber keeps files already exported; whether they must be deleted depends on the DSA.

sources.quote: you retain access to any files that you already exported
Review your Data Subscription Agreement to verify if your agreement requires that you delete exported data

claims.statement: The provider decides per offer whether subscribers get none, some or all historical revisions, and may also grant future revisions published during the subscription.

sources.quote: they give you access to 0 or more historical revisions, up to all historical revisions
They can also give you access to future revisions that are made available during your subscription period.

claims.statement: Subscribers to file products can auto-export new revisions to up to five of their own S3 buckets when the provider publishes them.

value.basis: maximum number of subscriber-owned buckets for automatic export of new revisions, Files products

sources.quote: automatically export new revisions to your Amazon S3 buckets (up to five buckets maximum)

claims.statement: Some products include data dictionaries and samples that prospective subscribers can view and download before subscribing.

sources.quote: you can view and download the data dictionaries and samples before you subscribe to it

claims.statement: If a provider indicates a product contains sensitive or personal data categories, this is displayed with the product details.

sources.quote: If the data provider has indicated that the product contains any categories of sensitive or personal data

claims.statement: When a buyer subscribes to a data product AWS may share the buyer's contact information with the provider.

sources.quote: When you subscribe to a data product, we might share your contact information with the provider.

claims.statement: For a data product with an upfront commitment the subscriber is invoiced by Amazon Web Services immediately.

sources.quote: you will receive an invoice from Amazon Web Services (AWS) immediately

claims.statement: AWS Data Exchange became generally available on 13 November 2019.

sources.quote: AWS Data Exchange is now generally available

claims.statement: Since 14 December 2023 data owners can share data through AWS Data Exchange data grants without registering as AWS Marketplace sellers.

sources.quote: Data owners can now share data using AWS Data Exchange without registering as a AWS Marketplace seller.

claims.statement: Products containing Amazon S3 data access became generally available on 14 March 2023.

sources.quote: Subscribing to and publishing data products containing Amazon S3 data access is now generally available.

claims.statement: Since 15 March 2022 providers can revoke subscribers' access to a revision and delete the revision's assets.

sources.quote: Providers can revoke subscribers' access to a revision and delete the assets of the revision.

claims.statement: Providers can send subscribers notifications about data updates, delays, schema changes and deprecations (launched 31 October 2023).

sources.quote: Providers can send notifications corresponding to data updates, data delays, schema changes, and deprecations.

claims.statement: The AWS Data Exchange FAQ states that a provider must use a legal entity domiciled in the United States or an EU member state.

sources.quote: valid legal entity domiciled in the United States or a member state of the EU

claims.statement: The AWS Data Exchange FAQ says providers receive a monthly disbursement for subscriptions less fulfilment fees.

sources.quote: You will receive a disbursement for subscriptions less fulfillment fees once a month.

claims.statement: When a subscription is no longer active, AWS Data Exchange revokes the subscriber's entitlement to the provider's data.

sources.quote: AWS Data Exchange revokes that subscriber's entitlement to your data.

claims.statement: Private offers let a provider make a public product available to selected AWS customers with custom price, duration, payment schedule, DSA or refund policy.

sources.quote: set terms including price, duration, payment schedule, DSA, or refund policy

claims.statement: When a buyer subscribes to an S3 data access product, AWS Data Exchange provisions an S3 access point and updates its policies on the provider's behalf to grant read-only access.

sources.quote: AWS Data Exchange automatically provisions an Amazon S3 access point and updates its resource policies on your behalf

claims.statement: For S3 data access products the subscriber's permissions on the provider's bucket are revoked when the subscription ends.

sources.quote: When the subscription ends, the subscriber’s permissions are revoked.

claims.statement: Objects shared through S3 data access must be in the S3 Standard storage class or managed by S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

sources.quote: Your shared objects must be in the Amazon S3 Standard Storage class, or be managed using S3 Intelligent Tiering

claims.statement: An S3 data access data set can share an entire bucket or up to five prefixes or objects within one bucket.

value.unit: prefixes or objects per S3 data access share
value.basis: maximum locations selectable within one bucket per data access share; whole bucket also allowed

sources.quote: specify up to five prefixes or objects within an Amazon S3 bucket

claims.statement: A provider sharing S3 data in place does not need to create a new revision when it updates the shared objects.

sources.quote: You don't need to create a new revision when updating the shared Amazon S3 objects

claims.statement: A provider can attach up to 10 samples of at most 50 MB to a product; CSV samples can be previewed.

value.basis: maximum number of provider-uploaded samples, 50 MB maximum size

sources.quote: You can upload up to 10 samples with a maximum size of 50 MB.

claims.statement: After a provider submits a product with a public offer, its status is Awaiting approval until AWS Data Exchange publishes it.

sources.quote: AWS Data Exchange prepares and publishes your product.

claims.statement: A private offer names at least one subscriber account and carries an offer expiration date by which the subscriber must accept.

sources.quote: add at least one subscriber account to which you want to extend the offer
by which the subscriber must accept the offer

claims.statement: Products can be set to Restricted, which stops new subscriptions and hides the product while existing allowlisted users keep using it.

sources.quote: it will no longer be visible to the public or available to new users

claims.statement: PIXTA AI's listing describes its sample as limited images with thumbnails for visual check only.

scope.product: Car dataset in multiple scenes for AI & Computer Vision

sources.quote: The sample set includes limited images with thumbnail for visual check only.

sources.quote: to start using our tailored services to help ideate, curate and customize datasets for your unique business needs

scope.product: Free Sample Dataset - 1000 High Resolution Images & Metadata

sources.quote: has_model_release

claims.statement: InfoBay AI's image dataset listing is sample data only, with enterprise licensing of the complete corpus available on request.

scope.product: Multidomain Image Dataset for Computer Vision & Multimodal AI

claims.statement: SilverLining.Cloud's currency history data product shows a public price of USD 370 for a 12-month contract.

scope.product: Currency Exchange Historical Data (140+ currencies)

value.basis: public offer list price paid by buyer, Product Access dimension, 12-month contract

claims.statement: AWS Marketplace sellers in India can create offers for AWS Data Exchange product types.

sources.quote: You can create products and offers for SaaS, AMI, Containers, Professional Services, ML and AWS Data Exchange product types.

claims.statement: AWS Marketplace sellers in India can only sell to buyers in India.

sources.quote: Sellers in India can only sell to buyers in India.

sources.quote: AWS India facilitates issuing GST tax invoices to buyers with you as the seller on record (SoR)

claims.statement: AWS says usage of data products sold on AWS Marketplace is governed by agreements between buyers and sellers to which AWS is not a party.

sources.quote: AWS is not a party to these agreements.

claims.statement: AWS says AWS Data Exchange has more than 3,500 products from over 300 providers.

value.basis: vendor-stated catalogue size, over 300 providers; undated page

sources.quote: AWS Data Exchange is the only data marketplace with more than 3,500 products from over 300 providers

claims.statement: VentureBeat reported, citing Amazon, that more than 80 providers contributed over 1,000 data products at launch in November 2019.

value.basis: providers at launch, as stated by Amazon and relayed by press; over 1,000 products

sources.quote: More than 80 data providers have contributed over 1,000 products containing data at launch, Amazon says.

claims.statement: A buyer who cannot find a product can request personalised recommendations from the AWS Data Exchange Data Discovery Team, which aims to respond within 2 business days.

sources.quote: You should receive a response from the AWS Data Exchange Data Discovery Team within 2 business days.

claims.statement: A data product request lets the buyer state delivery cadence, subscription length and subscription budget.

sources.quote: Delivery cadence

claims.statement: AWS's data consultation page says additional custom products are available through private products.

sources.quote: Additional custom products available through private products

claims.statement: A buyer can browse the AWS Data Exchange catalogue by category and filter by data set type, including Access to Amazon S3.

sources.quote: Products containing Amazon S3 data access

claims.statement: A data grant names the recipient's AWS account ID and can optionally be given an end date on which it expires.

sources.quote: optionally set an end date on which the data grant should expire

claims.statement: AWS Marketplace deducts the listing fee from the amount it disburses to the seller.

sources.quote: AWS Marketplace deducts this listing fee from the amount disbursed to the ISV.

claims.statement: Data set descriptions are visible only to recipients or subscribers with an active data grant or subscription.

sources.quote: The description is visible to recipients or subscribers who have an active data grant or subscription to the product.

sources.quote: AWS Data Exchange is a service that helps AWS customers easily share and manage data entitlements

sources.quote: charges for any AWS services you choose to store, process, or analyze the data products
